about: Toyota and Lexus enhanced sensors, from owner forums (Torque Pro / OBD Fusion users). Toyota doesn't publish these; every entry is unverified and model-specific. Some posters gave the temperature in °F; the formulas here convert their equations to °C so the app's unit setting works. Use "Check factory sensors on this car" and compare with coolant temperature after a drive before trusting a reading.

sensors.name: Transmission fluid temp (pan)
sensors.note: Reported working on 2016+ Tacoma V6 automatics (header 701, 2-3 owners on tacomaworld.com, transmission temperature PID thread). Not working on the 4-cylinder per one owner. Converted from the posted °F equation (A*459/255)+(B*1.6/255)-40.

sensors.name: Transmission fluid temp (after converter)
sensors.note: Same source as the pan sensor: 2016+ Tacoma V6, header 701. Unverified elsewhere.

sensors.name: Transmission fluid temp (2182, converter)
sensors.note: One owner (2018 Tacoma 2.6 I4 automatic, tacomaworld.com) posted ((C*256+D)*(7/100)-400)/10 in °F with no header given; 7E1 (transmission) is assumed here. Didn't work for a V6 owner. If it reads strangely, the original may have been °C.

sensors.name: Transmission fluid temp (Lexus ES, 2182)
sensors.note: One owner of a 2013-2018 Lexus ES (clublexus.com) reported it accurate, posted in °F: ((A*256+B)*(84/1000)-480)/12, header 7E1.
